items.notes: Arun, 3 Nov 2026: "best practices for FAST API, controllers, services, repository and whatever is the latest and greatest. Proper Gates using ruff, black etc". The package is layered api -> services -> repositories -> domain (ARCHITECTURE 12.1), enforced by import-linter; ruff format stands in for Black (compatible); the gates are scripts/backend_gates.sh, run by pre-commit, jira-flow and CI's Backend job. Then: "I need to code to be structured backend/ web/ ios/ infra/": the package, its tests and pyproject.toml live in backend/, and every record names backend/src/mypaisa_agent/.

items.summary: CI runs every gate, scan and Terraform plan on every pull request, the way smart-clearance does
items.notes: CI also runs the evals: T0 on every pull request, T1 when a prompt, tool, guard, model route or kind changes, T2 on a model change (MA-246, MA-250, MA-251; ARCHITECTURE 21.3). Settled: How ci-plan refreshes secrets without being able to read them (Arun, 24 Nov 2026): a separate secrets root. Every SSM parameter, secret or id, lives in infra/modules/secrets, called by infra/dev-secrets and infra/prod-secrets with their own state (mypaisa-agent/<env>/secrets.tfstate); infra/dev and infra/prod hold none, so ci-plan never plans one. ci-plan reads configuration, never contents: explicit denies on every parameter value in the account (ssm:GetParameter*), every kms:Decrypt but Lambda's own (MA-349), every S3 object but the two plan states and the lock files, DynamoDB items, Cognito users, log lines and secret values (ARCHITECTURE 17.4). The laptop plans and applies dev-secrets through tf.sh; prod-secrets is planned and applied only by the release (MA-107).

items.summary: Terraform builds dev and prod as two isolated environments in one account, applied only from CI through OIDC
items.notes: Settled: Who puts prod's secret values (Arun, 24 Nov 2026, MA-26): the developer role's one exception to its env=prod deny is ssm:PutParameter on /mypaisa-agent/prod/*, for Arun to put prod's secret values by hand; it never reads, decrypts, deletes or tags a prod parameter, and Claude never runs it. Build note for infra/bootstrap: an explicit deny beats any allow, so the exception is cut out of the deny itself (the env=prod deny names every action but ssm:PutParameter, and a second deny refuses ssm:PutParameter on anything tagged env=prod outside /mypaisa-agent/prod/*), never added as an allow beside it; the overwrite needs no ssm:AddTagsToResource, which stays denied. Built 24 Nov 2026: plans for bootstrap (18 to add), dev (37) and prod (36) clean; scripts/infra_guard_check.py proves the guard in IAM's simulator (25 cases, 0 wrong; a guard without the exception fails it). ci-plan's ability to decrypt secrets is an open question on MA-25, whose plan job is the first to assume ci-plan.

Settled: Which phase holds the first prod release (Arun, 24 Nov 2026): phase 0. MA-107 builds the release pipeline in phase 0, and its first run applies prod's empty stack (infra/prod and infra/prod-secrets) after Arun approves; Arun then puts prod's secret values, so MA-142 and the prod halves of MA-21 and MA-143 finish in phase 0, and MA-108's nightly drift check watches prod from then on. The first Lambdas reach prod in phase 1 through the same pipeline. The smoke tests: a release that ships no Lambda runs its read-only smoke against the placeholders; a release that ships a Lambda refuses prod while any /mypaisa-agent/prod/* parameter is still at version 1, the placeholder Terraform wrote, read with DescribeParameters, which shows the version and never a value. Built 24 Nov 2026: release.yml starts when CI passes on a push to main (workflow_run) and ships only when the commit changes something a release ships since the commit prod last ran (GitHub's prod deployments). Dev applies dev-secrets and dev with ci-dev-deploy; ci-plan plans infra/prod before any approval and writes it to the run's summary with its digest; after Arun approves, the prod job plans again and refuses a plan whose digest is not the one he read, refuses a secrets plan that does anything but create a parameter or change its tags (any other change to an existing parameter sends an empty value or the placeholder over the value put by hand), refuses a release that ships a Lambda while a prod parameter is at version 1, applies, publishes and moves the live aliases, and runs the read-only smoke (scripts/smoke.py: the table, the buckets and the parameters, by describe, get and list calls only); a failed smoke moves every alias back. items.summary: Two of MA-194's fixed-finding checks run in web/ at the same time and race, so Review tooling fails at random
items.notes: Found on 23 Nov 2026 on Dependabot's web group, PR #113 (MA-326): Review tooling failed MA-194 r1-f1 with 'No such file or directory (os error 2)' while r1-f7 passed. review_regress.py --every --jobs 4 ran check.sh's service-worker and money-compact at once in a checkout with no web/node_modules; pnpm 12 installs before an exec when node_modules is missing, and both did so in the same folder. Reproduced on main locally, where the second try failed with ENOTEMPTY on Vite's optimizer cache under web/node_modules/.vite, which both vitest runs write. Main had passed by timing. check.sh now takes one flock per checkout around every command that runs in web/ or copies it; the lock goes when its holder dies, so a check killed by its timeout never leaves it held. A harness makes no failure of its own (lesson 16).

items.summary: CodeQL scans Swift only when a pull request changes ios/, from a cached build, so other pull requests no longer wait about 28 minutes
items.notes: Filed 24 Nov 2026 (Arun: "why is Analyze Swift takes so much time ?" ... "Yes, file it"). Measured on PR #129: 10 min queued for a macos-latest runner, 17 min 41 s of CodeQL autobuild tracing a cold Xcode build of ios/MyPaisa.xcodeproj, 1 min 20 s of analysis; PR #128's took 17 min, and main's at 17:00 was cancelled at exactly 15 min. Built 24 Nov 2026 (Arun: "I need Option 1 to be done fast"): .github/workflows/codeql.yml; the default setup's job log showed its autobuild failing on the app (the React Native packages need pnpm spm first) and falling back until it compiled only MyPaisaCore and MyPaisaUI, so the Swift job builds the MyPaisaUI package by hand (MyPaisaCore with it) on macos-26, the runner and Xcode 26.6 the default setup used, caching only the Swift package checkouts so CodeQL still sees every compile of our own code; default setup switched off in the repository's settings.

items.notes: Filed on MA-355 (25 Nov 2026). Picked there by Arun: d 1a, watcher at work. Its boards are Mark in motion in ds-v1 and iPhone v4 · Mark in motion. It extends MA-103's intro on ds-v1 Logo (the pound now draws itself, and the dot travels on the new easing). One easing, --mo-travel, and the mo-logo-* keyframes joined motion.css in the three board folders; under Reduce Motion nothing travels. On the web only the sidebar's mark moves; on iPhone the mark beside the reply does. Nothing moves on phone web. For the build: motion.css's own Reduce Motion rule lands every keyframe at once, so the dim and the still ring need to be 150 ms opacity transitions or pinned durations. Settled: The lap under the dim (Arun, 25 Nov 2026, asked on MA-355's PR): the chat sheet dims the page, not the sidebar, so the lap and the ring are seen beside the open chat. Settled: The iPhone chat's mark (Arun, 25 Nov 2026): the coin mark sits beside each of MyPaisa's messages on iPhone and iPad, as on the web, and does the lap and the ring; the iOS kit and the chat boards are redrawn with it before this story starts. Built on stubbed data, web only (Arun, 25 Nov 2026: the web app first, then iOS): the sidebar's mark, live, from DS v1 · Mark in motion. It arrives once per load (about 1.1 s, the name after it), laps once when MyPaisa's turn starts on a member's message (1.2 s), and rings once when a change is saved (0.6 s): a Confirm, plan or check-in saved in the chat, or a figure saved in place on a page (any wealth mutation). One movement at a time, none while the tab is hidden, nothing loops; Reduce Motion fades in place. Filled by judgement (Arun, 25 Nov 2026: "Fill in by judgement"), to be checked by eye: the ring on a figure saved in place on a web page; a member who is not an admin laps and never rings, since only their own saves ring; nothing changes at 1280. Not built here: the iOS launch, the coin mark beside iOS chat messages, the iPad.
